summary.text: Paleoclimatology is the scientific study of climates from before weather instruments were invented, when no direct measurements were taken.
It gathers clues preserved in rocks, sediments, ice sheets, tree rings, corals, shells and microfossils, then dates them to work out past states of the atmosphere.
Because instrument records cover only a tiny part of Earth's history, rebuilding ancient climates helps explain natural variation and how today's climate came about.

facts.label: Longest ice record
facts.value: Over 800,000 years, from the EPICA project

facts.label: Instrument records begin
facts.value: Mid-1800s, giving about 150 years of data

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know what the air itself was made of 100,000 years ago. Why are ice cores so useful for this?

options.label: Ice keeps absorbing gases from the air above it
Ice changes color to match the air's makeup
Ice melts at a rate set by the old air
Snow seals air in bubbles as it turns to ice

items.explain: As snow is pressed into ice under later snowfall, air gets locked in small bubbles that can be measured directly.

items.prompt: Deep-sea sediments are a rich climate record, yet none on the ocean floor are older than about 200 million years. Why?

options.label: Ocean plates are eventually subducted
Seawater dissolves sediments over time
Earlier oceans had no sediments at all
Drills cannot reach deeper layers

items.explain: The deep marine record sits on oceanic plates, which are eventually subducted, taking the oldest material with them.

items.prompt: An ice layer holds a higher ratio of oxygen-18 to oxygen-16 than the layer below it. Setting other factors aside, what does that point to?

options.label: Colder ocean surface at the time
Warmer ocean surface at the time
A larger volcanic eruption
The layer is simply younger

items.explain: Water with heavy oxygen-18 evaporates at higher temperatures, so the ratio rises as temperature rises.

items.prompt: In the 1600s, Robert Hooke studied fossils of giant turtles found in Dorset, England. What did he conclude?

options.label: A great flood carried them there
Turtles once lived in cold seas
Dorset once had a warmer climate
The fossils were carved by people

items.explain: Hooke argued only a once warmer climate could explain them, which he thought came from a shift in Earth's axis.

items.prompt: How can scientists tell which depth in an ice core matches which stretch of time?

options.label: Deeper ice is always the same age
Seasonal pauses leave visible layers
Ice color fades at a fixed rate
Bubbles grow larger with each year

items.explain: Snow builds up with seasonal pauses, so layers form that can be tied to ranges of time.

items.prompt: Why do very old sediments usually give less reliable climate data than younger ones?

options.label: They hold too much pollen to count
Older climates changed too slowly
They were never buried deep enough
Pressure, tectonics and fluids alter them

items.explain: Millions of years of pressure, tectonic activity and fluid flow corrupt older sediments, lowering the quality and resolution of their data.
